intro.author: 'Jude… brother of James' (v. 1), traditionally Judas, a brother of Jesus and James (Mark 6:3). Some scholars think a later writer used his name.
intro.written: Uncertain; often dated somewhere between the AD 50s and 80s
intro.audience: Believers 'sanctified… preserved… and called' (v. 1), not named, probably Christians familiar with Jewish writings and traditions
intro.setting: Certain people had 'crept in unawares' (v. 4) and were taking part in the church's fellowship meals while turning God's grace into an excuse for immorality and rejecting authority. Jude had planned to write about the salvation they shared but felt he must urge them instead to 'contend for the faith' (v. 3). He draws on well-known Jewish traditions, including the book of 1 Enoch.
intro.purpose: Jude warns against false teachers, reminds readers that God judges ungodliness, and urges them to keep themselves in God's love.
intro.bigIdea: Contend for the faith, and trust the God who is able to keep you from falling.

outline.title: Warning against intruders, and a call to persevere
